title: kbmon's live view keeps one CPU core busy the whole time it runs
goal: Found 2026-10-18 from the operator's report of high load: a live kbmon.py --interval 5 used 29 CPU seconds in 30 s of wall time (with its child processes), and the operator's own kbmon had run at ~100% CPU for 39 minutes. The live view's work per interval (the kb panel ~5 s, the sessions panel ~5 s, coord calls) is as long as the interval, and the resize poll may add a busy wait. After the fix the live view idles between refreshes: the next refresh starts an interval after the last one finished, slow panels whose inputs did not change are served from their last result (kb counts change only on a commit), the resize wait blocks instead of spinning, and a 30 s live run at --interval 5 uses under 6 CPU seconds; --once and --json are unchanged.

run:
import os,pty,sys,time,select,signal,resource
pid,fd=pty.fork()
if pid==0:
    os.execvp(sys.executable,[sys.executable,"_tools/kbmon.py","--interval","5"])
t=time.time()
while time.time()-t<30:
    r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.5)
    if r:
        try: os.read(fd,65536)
        except OSError: break
os.kill(pid,signal.SIGTERM); os.waitpid(pid,0)
u=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN); cpu=u.ru_utime+u.ru_stime
print("kbmon cpu seconds in 30 s of live view:",round(cpu,1))
sys.exit(0 if cpu<6 else 1)
